- **Affected part**: Corn ear with husks pulled back
- **Key features**: Gray-green discolored interior visible through husks; appears to be mold/discoloration on kernels
- **Primary candidates**: Ear rot diseases (likely Aspergillus, Trichoderma, or Diplodia based on gray-green coloration)

| Disease | Key Features | Match to Test |
|---------|-------------|---------------|
| **Aspergillus** | Olive-green to gray-green powdery mold | ✓ BEST MATCH |

| Diplodia | White mold, grayish-brown (base start) | Wrong color profile |
| Gibberella | Pinkish-white, red kernel streaking | Wrong color |
| Fusarium | White to pink/salmon cottony mold | Wrong color |

**Analysis:**
The test image shows a gray-green discolored area visible within the ear husks. This coloration and appearance most closely match **Aspergillus ear rot**, which is characterized by:
- Olive-green to gray-green powdery mold (matches the visible discoloration)
- Commonly visible when husks are pulled back
- Powdery/dusty appearance consistent with what's visible in the test image

The gray-green tone distinctly differentiates this from Trichoderma (darker green/blue), Diplodia (white/grayish-brown), Gibberella (pink/red), and Fusarium (white/pink).
